paragraphs: 1. Avot, chapter 4. Mishnah Kilayim 9:8; Sotah 9:13; Kiddushin 4:14; Bava Metzia 2:1; Avodah Zarah 4:11; Makhshirin 4:1, 6:7.

2. Yuhasin writes in the order of the generations: it appears that he was the son of R' Elazar ben Perata. It seems to me that this is not so, for in Sanhedrin 22a and Jerusalem Megillah 1:11 [the parallel in the checked edition is at 1:9:4], R' Shimon ben Elazar reports in R' Elazar ben Perata's name. In Ta'anit, chapter 3, 20 end of side a: when he came from Migdal Eder, from his teacher’s house [the checked Bavli reads Migdal Gedor], he was very happy because he had learned much Torah. He encountered an exceedingly ugly person. Rashi—and Tosafot in the name of Massekhet Derekh Eretz—writes that this was Eliyahu, who intended to rebuke him so that he would not become accustomed to this behavior. He said to him, “Empty one! Are all the people of your town like this?” He answered, “Go to the Craftsman who made me.” He appeased him at length until he forgave him, on condition that he not make a habit of it. He went forth and expounded, “A person should always be soft like a reed.” Our reading is R' Elazar ben Shimon, and in Ein Yaakov R' Elazar son of R' Shimon. But the Rif in Ein Yaakov writes R' Shimon ben Elazar, as do Avot de-Rabbi Natan, chapter 41, and Derekh Eretz, chapter 4. His burial is at Shezuri; see R' Yishmael ben Elisha the high priest.

3. In R' Elazar ben Perata's name; see above. In the name of ראב״צ [Keritut 20a reads R. Eliezer son of R. Tzadok]: Keritut 20a. In Shabbat 95a, in R' Eliezer's name. With R' Elazar ha-Kappar. R' Hiyya the Great reports in his name: Middot. In Halafta ben Agra's name. R' Yehudah son of R' Simon reports in his name. R' Yehudah was his teacher. R' Yohanan said, “I was riding on my grandfather's shoulder and heard R' Shimon ben Elazar's voice as he sat teaching, ‘They put into a cucumber's interior …’”: Jerusalem Ma'asrot, first chapter, halakhah 2. Perhaps this is R' Yohanan the tanna; see R' Yohanan. He disagrees with R' Yose ben Meshullam. In R' Yose the Galilean's name. In Hullin, first chapter, 6 beginning of side a, R' Meir sent him to bring wine from the Samaritans. An old man encountered him; Tosafot write that it was Eliyahu, and so forth. He went and told R' Meir, and so forth; see Rav Yitzhak bar Yosef. He bathed with R' Meir: Jerusalem Kirah, halakhah 3. He said that R' Meir wrote a Megillah from memory; see his entry. He prepared a remedy for R. Meir when he was ill [the Bavli says Meir declined it]; see his entry. In R' Meir's name: Sotah, Arusah; Shabbat 154, end of side b; Sukkah 35; Pesahim 37; Bava Kamma 69; Bava Metzia 50, 78, 90; Helek 103b; Kiddushin 24a, 47 end of side a, 57; Hullin 6, 33b; Menahot 30b, 31 end of side b. Tosafot there write: it is puzzling, for R' Shimon ben Elazar appears to have been R' Meir's pupil, since he often reports in his name. But in Shabbat 79, end of side b, R' Shimon ben Elazar said, “Meir used to write it on parchment,” implying he was his colleague, since he said Meir, not R' Meir. Perhaps all the books have a scribal error. If we were to say that there were two R' Shimon ben Elazars, it would be satisfactory; see his entry. Our reading is R' Meir.

In Jerusalem Megallehin, halakhah 1: R' Shimon son of Rabbi found no opening for his vow until one of the elders of Galilee came. Some say it was R' Shimon ben Elazar, and so forth. He asked, “Whence do you know it?” He answered, “I was R' Meir's attendant.” Some say R' Meir's staff was in his hand, and it taught him understanding. So too there in Nedarim, beginning of chapter 9; see the commentary there, at 73, and above, R' Meir. In Tosafot, Bava Metzia 4b: although R' Shimon ben Elazar was R' Akiva's pupil, there is no concern in his disagreeing with him and being mentioned first, for we find something similar with two people holding a document, where Rabbi disputes his father Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, and so forth; see my lengthy discussion in the rules. Tosafot object concerning books that read R' Akiva: if so, R' Akiva's words contradict each other. Some books read R' Yaakov, not R' Akiva. End of quotation. So too it appears, for nowhere in the Talmud do we find R' Shimon ben Elazar [contextual proposal; digital witness ראב״ש] reporting in R' Akiva's name, except in Tosefta Ma'asrot, end of chapter 2, in R' Akiva's name. There, in Gittin, chapter 2: a woman herself brings her bill of divorce, by an a fortiori argument, ‘If her rival-wife ….’ In Tosefta Temurah, beginning of chapter 1: R' Akiva's words; R' Shimon ben Elazar says. In Gittin 23b, R' Shimon ben Elazar reports in R' Akiva's name. Moreover, he was R' Meir's pupil, and R' Meir was R' Akiva's pupil. How could he dispute his teacher's teacher and be placed before him? Shmuel reports in his name: Ketubbot 10, beginning of side a. Rav Shmuel bar Yitzhak reports in his name: Midrash Kohelet Rabbah. He testified in R' Shimon ben Hananyah's name. In R' Shimon ben Yohai's name: Shabbat 49a; Horayot 9, 12; Yoma 5a; Hullin 5, beginning of side b. In R' Shimon ben Yehotzadak's name: Jerusalem Pesahim 2:3—requires examination.
